items.title: Brunei, Malaysia to strengthen cross-border security, SAR cooperation
items.summary: In a joint statement issued by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah following the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation between the two countries in Bandar Seri Begawan, the two leaders said cross-border security issues needed to be addressed through closer cooperation between the relevant agencies of both sides. On cross-border SAR and emergency response, both leaders said the focus would be on enhancing coordination, exploring areas of collaboration and strengthening mutual understanding of cross-border arrangements, while building on existing cooperation in disaster management. Both leaders also acknowledged the importance of closer coordination in addressing cross-border disaster management and emergency response.

items.title: Anwar: No compromise on territorial rights in Malaysia-Brunei border talks
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 22 — The long-delayed Malaysia-Brunei border issue was among the topics discussed at the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) between the two countries today. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that, so far, the two countries have completed about 50 per cent of the border demarcation process. Anwar said ALC-27 between Malaysia and Brunei is the best platform to resolve outstanding issues and strengthen relations between the two countries.

items.title: China, Indonesia deepen defence ties, cooperation on minerals, energy and tech
items.summary: JAKARTA: China and Indonesia agreed on Friday to boost military ties and work closely on minerals, energy and technology, as Jakarta seeks to balance ties with both Beijing and Washington amid economic and geopolitical tensions, including in the South China Sea. Both countries should "seize the moment," China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in remarksmade at the start of his visit to Jakarta. "China actively aims to build China-Indonesia cooperation at a high level," Wang added.

items.title: Malaysia, Brunei target 2034 to complete border demarcation, Sector F-G by 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Brunei have agreed to jointly determine and demarcate the watershed in Sector F-G of their land boundary by May 31 next year, reaffirming that the issue must be resolved solely based on the watershed principle. In a joint statement, both leaders reiterated their commitment to the 2009 Exchange of Letters and other bilateral instruments governing the demarcation and survey of the land boundary. Malaysia and Brunei are also targeting completion of the joint survey and demarcation of their entire land boundary by 2034.

items.title: Fahmi: PM’s remarks on China and Taiwan consistent with Malaysia’s policy since Tun Razak’s time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Malaysia’s position on the China-Taiwan issue remains consistent and has never changed since the administration of former Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi said the position expressed by the prime minister was in line with and consistent with the country’s foreign policy maintained by Wisma Putra for many years. “The prime minister merely stated what is consistent with Wisma Putra’s position.

items.title: AUKU repeal to pave way for new higher education law
items.summary: KEPALA BATAS: The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) is not solely focused on students, as the government is also reviewing the entire higher education legal framework before introducing a new Act as its replacement. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the review was necessary as AUKU is the main legislation governing not only student-related matters but also the establishment and operations of universities, governance, academic affairs and administration. He said the new Act must serve as the main legal framework covering the entire higher education ecosystem, addressing both present and future needs.

items.title: Sarawak confirms 26 rabies cases this year, including three cats
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN, Aug 22 — Three cats were among 26 animals confirmed positive for rabies in Sarawak so far this year, with the remaining 23 cases involving dogs. Since July 2017, Sarawak has recorded 94 human rabies cases with 87 deaths, data verified with JKNS on Aug 20, 2026. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is almost universally fatal.

items.title: Kuantan jewellery heist over in 5 minutes, getaway bikes had no number plates
items.summary: KUANTAN: Four armed men took just five minutes to make off with RM500,000 worth of jewellery from a goldsmith's shop in Taman Pandan Damai here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the masked suspects arrived and fled on two motorcycles without number plates, believed to be part of an attempt to evade identification. Yesterday, the four suspects, armed with a parang and a suspected pump-action gun, entered the shop about 2pm and fled with jewellery worth RM500,000.

items.title: Renault Captur gutted by fire after crashing into Honda City on SPE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR — A Renault Captur sports utility vehicle (SUV) was completely destroyed by fire after colliding with a car on the Setiawangsa-Pantai Expressway (SPE) heading towards Mid Valley today. The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Control Centre received an emergency call via the MERS999 line at 12.37pm. In response, Operations Commander Senior Fire Officer I Muhammad Amirudin Mohd Hassan led a team of nine personnel from the Hang Tuah Fire and Rescue Station to the scene, deploying one Fire Rescue Tender and two Rapid Intervention Motorcycle units.

items.title: After past mishap, 88-year-old Melaka man takes no chances with Jalur Gemilang
items.summary: MELAKA: An 88-year-old Melaka man is taking no chances with the Jalur Gemilang this National Month, repeatedly contacting his assemblyman to ensure the national flag at his home is not displayed upside down again. George Lim, a Baba Nyonya from Taman Semabok Jaya, contacted Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem more than five times after a previous experience of having the Jalur Gemilang installed incorrectly left him deeply concerned about a repeat of the mistake. Noor Helmy said Lim remained traumatised by the previous incident but was determined to continue flying the national flag at his home.

items.title: Malaysia, Brunei deepen cooperation in border management, education, disaster response
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN: Malaysia and Brunei Darussalam have agreed to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including border management, immigration, education, disaster management, trade and investment. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said long-standing border issues between the two countries were also given priority during his discussions with Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah at Istana Nurul Iman here today. He said an initial understanding had been reached to ensure that areas agreed to belong to Brunei and Sarawak would be maintained, in line with the interests of both countries.

items.title: Homeowner loses RM25,000 in valuables in Bukit Antarabangsa break-in
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A homeowner lost about RM25,000 worth of valuables after a burglar broke into his house in Bukit Antarabangsa while he was at work yesterday. Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the victim discovered the break-in after checking his home's closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at about 4pm. "The footage showed a Perodua Myvi stopping in front of the house in Jalan Wangsa 5, Taman Wangsa Ukay, at noon.

items.title: Nearly RM1mil pumped into Gombak community, school projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A joint programme between the Selangor government and the Higher Education Ministry has channelled nearly RM1 million in funding towards community and school development in Gombak, says Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Amirudin, who is also Gombak MP, said the Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Madani programmes at Kampung Melayu Wira Damai and SMK Sungai Kertas respectively were implemented under the ministry's Higher Education Department, with funding from the department and private sector partners. Amirudin later said he was scheduled to visit Sekolah Agama Al-Amin, where an education carnival was being held.

items.title: Haze: 10 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 196
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 3pm today, with Serian recording the highest reading at 196. Based on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas recording unhealthy API readings included Kuching (188), Samarahan (178), Sri Aman (175) and Sarikei (174). Bukit Rambai in Melaka was the only area outside Sarawak to record an unhealthy API reading, at 152.

items.title: Selangor eyes RM2.5mil upgrade for Bukit Permata Muslim cemetery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor government plans to upgrade the Bukit Permata Muslim cemetery at an estimated cost of RM2.5 million, with the project to be proposed for next year's state budget. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the upgrade was expected to take about two years to complete. On the ongoing development of the Sungai Kertas Muslim cemetery in Sungai Tua, Amirudin said the first phase was on track for completion in October, with subsequent phases to follow.

items.title: Putrajaya cyclist deaths highlight need for stronger road safety measures
items.summary: Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA) founder and road safety and motorsports adviser Jamil Manan Supri said the deaths of Syazwan Zharif Abdul Karim, 30, and Mohd Hilmi Tahar, 48, should serve as a serious road safety lesson for all road users. Jamil said preventing similar incidents required a shared effort involving cyclists, motorists, road authorities and cycling groups or event organisers. Jamil also reminded motorists to anticipate vulnerable road users and not assume a road was clear simply because another vehicle or cyclist was not immediately visible.

items.title: Hiker found safe after 19 hours lost in Lambir Hills National Park
items.summary: MIRI: A female hiker who spent the night lost in Lambir Hills National Park was found safe today after a 19-hour search. Firefighters from the Miri Fire and Rescue Station, assisted by park rangers and Wildlife Guardian Rangers, were deployed for the search and rescue operation. Keywords: NST, News, Nation, Region, State, Sarawak, Miri, Missing, person, Fire and rescue department, search, woman, national park, Bukit Lambir, rangers, park, night, wildlife, Malaysia, hiking © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Amirudin to meet Anwar on PH-BN talks for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari will meet chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to discuss the possibility of PH and Barisan Nasional cooperating in the upcoming Melaka election. Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, said he was expected to meet Anwar tomorrow to discuss the matter. He, however, said no meeting had yet taken place with Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, but expected talks to progress following his discussion with the Prime Minister.

items.title: Sarawak firefighters conduct water bombing to battle third-day Lundu forest fire
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department today conducted a water-bombing operation to help extinguish a forest fire at the Samunsan Forest Reserve in Lundu, which entered its third day. The department said in a statement that the operation involved a helicopter from the Miri Fire and Rescue Air Unit. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department said updates on the firefighting operation and monitoring efforts would be provided from time to time.

items.title: Zambry: UUCA repeal requires holistic review of higher education law
items.summary: KEPALA BATAS, Aug 22 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 transcends the immediate interests of the student body, and requires a holistic review of the entire higher education legal framework before a replacement is drafted. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir explained that the review must be comprehensive because the UUCA serves as the primary legislation governing not only student conduct, but also the establishment, operation, and administration of universities, Bernama reported. “The current UUCA has 44 sections covering aspects of university establishment, university governance, academic standing, academic staff, administrators and others, with seven of those 44 sections relating to students,” Zambry said.

items.title: JAIS mulls police clearance screening for religious school teachers
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) is formulating measures and guidelines to curb sexual misconduct involving students at religious schools. Its director, Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, said discussions were underway with the School Registration Committee, with one of the proposals involving a more stringent teacher screening process. Shahzihan said guidelines governing interactions between students and teachers were also being discussed, including proposals for stricter segregation.

items.title: Sabah labour market shows improvement amid strong sectoral growth, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's labour market has shown improving trends, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He added that the construction sector recorded the highest growth at 28.3 per cent, followed by manufacturing at five per cent, mining and quarrying at 4.9 per cent, and services at 4.5 per cent. Also present were Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar and Malaysia Petroleum Management senior vice-president Datuk Bacho Pilong.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching: 99,693 scam posts removed as of July 15, surpassing 2025 figures
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 22 — A total of 99,693 pieces of scam-related content on social media platforms were removed as of July 15 this year, exceeding the 98,503 taken down throughout 2025. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said 106,268 requests had been submitted to social media platforms such as Meta, TikTok and YouTube to remove such content during the same period, compared with 102,113 requests throughout last year. Teo said the campaign was also aimed at reminding the public to fly the Jalur Gemilang correctly.

items.title: Sarawak postpones National Day events as haze pushes API readings to unhealthy levels statewide
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 22 — The Sarawak-level National Day Celebration 2026 and two other major events have been postponed as a precaution amid unhealthy air quality in several parts of the state, said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. Other stations recording unhealthy air quality were Kuching (185), Lundu and Lubok Antu (179 each), Samarahan (177), Sri Aman and Sarikei (174 each), Sibu (163), Bintulu and Mukah (157 each), Samalaju (156), Tebedu (153), Miri (151) and Lawas (109). Uggah said organisers of other public activities and events, particularly outdoor programmes and mass gatherings, were also advised to postpone them to a suitable date to reduce public exposure to unhealthy air quality.

items.title: Sarawak taska to close when API reaches 200, says Nancy
items.summary: KUCHING: Childcare centres (taska) in Sarawak will be closed when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, in line with a decision previously made by the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC). Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the measure was aimed at protecting children from exposure to haze, which could affect their health. On concerns among working parents should childcare centres be closed, Nancy said the matter would have to be managed by the respective state governments as the directive fell under state jurisdiction.

items.title: Japan dad ditches 7-year-old for hours to climb Mt Fuji
items.summary: TOKYO: A man left his seven-year-old son behind for hours on Japan's Mount Fuji while continuing his climb, resulting in a stern warning from authorities, police and local media reported. The boy was found alone on a hiking route on Thursday and taken into police custody, a local police officer in the Shizuoka region told AFP on Saturday. The police officer told AFP that officers gave the man a telling-off for leaving the child behind.

items.title: Nearly 100,000 scam-related social media content removed this year
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A total of 99,693 pieces of scam-related content on social media platforms were removed as of July 15 this year, exceeding the 98,503 taken down throughout 2025. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said 106,268 requests had been submitted to social media platforms such as Meta, TikTok and YouTube to remove scam-related content during the same period, compared with 102,113 requests throughout last year. Teo said the campaign also aimed to remind the public to fly the Jalur Gemilang correctly.

items.title: Sarawak childcare centres to shut once haze hits API 200, Nancy Shukri confirms directive
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 22 — Childcare centres (taska) in Sarawak will be closed immediately if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, in line with the decision previously made by the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC). Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the measure was aimed at protecting children from exposure to haze, which could affect their health. On Aug 12, the SDMC said in a statement that schools, kindergartens and childcare centres would be closed immediately when the API reached 200, classified as the very unhealthy level, in accordance with the National Haze Action Plan and under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak Education Department director.

items.title: Teluk Intan student awarded RM129,040 after bubur lambuk mishap leaves scars, lasting trauma
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Aug 22 — A secondary school student has been awarded RM129,040 in damages after the Sessions Court here found her school and two teachers liable for negligence over an incident in which she was scalded by boiling porridge during a programme in 2022. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), Judge Gan Peng Kun ruled yesterday that the defendants failed in their duty of care by allowing a mathematics class to be held inside the cooking area and by delaying the girl’s transfer to hospital following the accident at SK Seri Intan. The suit was filed in 2024 by the girl’s mother, M. Thanaletchumi, who named the headmaster, two teachers and the government as defendants.

items.title: SUV catches fire after hitting car on Setiawangsa-Pantai Expressway
items.summary: The City Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received a distress call at 12.37pm. The fire was extinguished at 1.21pm. It said nine firefighters from the Hang Tuah Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene in a Fire Rescue Tender and on two Rapid Intervention Motorcycles.

items.title: Bentong council, DoE identifying culprits behind alleged waste dumping
items.summary: BENTONG: The Bentong Municipal Council (MPB) is working with the Department of Environment (DOE) to identify factories and contractors allegedly responsible for dumping suspected chemical waste at an industrial area here. He said the council would also cooperate with the Department of Irrigation and Drainage, if necessary, while working to identify the lorries transporting the waste. It was reported yesterday that a resident claimed a vacant area in the Bentong industrial area had been turned into a dumping ground for various types of waste, including chemicals.

items.title: Trump predicts impeachment if Democrats win midterms
items.summary: WASHINGTON: United States (US) President Donald Trump said Democrats would try to impeach him if they win the midterm elections in November and gain control of Congress, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. I'm going to have to go through impeachment," Trump said at a rally in South Carolina. They have no idea why," Trump said.

items.title: Nuclear technology holds potential to boost food security
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: The development of new crop varieties using nuclear technology could contribute to Malaysia's food security, although the research process before commercialisation usually takes several generations to ensure seed stability. "For example, one generation of nuclear cassava takes between six and nine months, compared with existing cassava varieties. This allows nuclear cassava to produce higher yields within a shorter period.

items.title: PH committed to fair MP allocations, but consensus needed, says Aiman Athirah
items.summary: Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the provision of allocations should be underpinned by a clear legal framework, including comprehensive guidelines on distribution mechanisms and monitoring systems. The current government is a unity government formed by various political parties with different histories, struggles and manifestos. Aiman Athirah said fair and equitable constituency allocations remained central to PH's reform agenda.

items.title: Driver ploughs into food court, woman killed
items.summary: KAJANG: A 47-year-old woman was killed after a car crashed into a food court at Bandar Mahkota Cheras here early today. Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the incident occurred about 1.15pm. Preliminary investigations found that the 35-year-old Malaysian driver is believed to have accidentally pressed the accelerator, causing his car to crash into the dining area of the food court.

items.title: Pas: Anwar should have urged for peaceful dialogue on Taiwan-China issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should have called for peaceful dialogue and urged restraint over the Taiwan-China issue rather than appear to advocate the use of force, a Pas leader said. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Malaysia should adopt a more cautious position on the China-Taiwan conflict and not allow itself to be seen as taking sides with any major power. "Pas said there was no issue with the Prime Minister's reiteration of Malaysia's position on the One China policy.

items.title: MPH contributes RM19,533 to Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: MPH Bookstores has contributed RM19,533.44 from its Mutiara Minda 2026 campaign to the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund. Previous campaigns supported orphanages and other beneficiaries, but proceeds were channelled to the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund this year. The Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund provides financial assistance to underprivileged Malaysians needing critical medical treatment and surgery, while supporting other vulnerable groups.

items.title: Falling pole kills woman trying to stop fleeing driver in Bandar Mahkota food court
items.summary: KAJANG, Aug 22 — A 47-year-old woman was killed instantly when a falling pole struck her during a chaotic attempt to stop an errant driver at a food court in Bandar Mahkota, Cheras. The tragedy unfolded on Thursday, Aug 22, when a 35-year-old male driver accidentally pressed his accelerator pedal, sending his vehicle crashing directly into the food court’s dining area, The Star reported. However, the vehicle collided with a nearby pole, causing the structure to topple directly onto the woman.

items.title: Anwar conferred royal honour from Brunei Sultan
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was today conferred the Darjah Kerabat Laila Utama Yang Amat Dihormati (D.K.) by the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. Also present were Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan; Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani; Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg; and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

items.title: Lawyer who represented Anwar in black eye incident dies at 81
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran lawyer Chew Swee Yoke, a pioneer of legal aid in Malaysia who represented Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in proceedings linked to his infamous black-eye incident, has died at the age of 81. Her daughter, celebrity chef and Bistro à Table owner Isadora Chai, announced her mother's death in an Instagram post, saying Chew died on Aug 20. In 1982, Chew established Kuala Lumpur's first Legal Aid Centre and became the inaugural chairman of the Bar Council Legal Aid Committee.

items.title: Sultan of Brunei confers highest family order award on Anwar
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was today conferred the Darjah Kerabat Laila Utama Yang Amat Dihormati (D.K.) by the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. Also present were Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan; Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani; Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg; and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

items.title: Penang launches ONEMAP+ to track CCTVs, AEDs, and EV chargers across the state
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — The Penang state government has launched ONEMAP+, a new digital platform designed to map the locations of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras, automated external defibrillators (AEDs), and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations across the state. One platform, many benefits,” Chow said. Developed by PLANMalaysia Penang and the state Information and Communications Technology Division, the initiative incorporates data from the Penang Green Council, the Penang Island City Council (MBPP), the Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), and the Penang Health Department.

items.title: Penang Port Commission says ferry ridership up 7pc in first half of 2026, announces free Merdeka rides
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — Penang’s ferry services recorded a 7.28 per cent increase in passenger traffic between January and June this year compared to the same period in 2025. Penang Port Commission chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said that passenger volume in June alone reached 262,424. “These figures clearly reflect the sustained demand for ferry services as a key mode of public transportation in the state,” Yeoh said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia presses Asean for collective action on transboundary haze as El Niño peaks
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 22 — Malaysia is calling for collective action from all Asean member states to enhance preparedness in addressing the risk of transboundary haze through preventive measures, national preparedness and continuous monitoring, based on the principles of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said all member states needed to strengthen control measures and preparedness by maintaining close monitoring of high-risk areas, enhancing hotspot surveillance, strengthening enforcement of the ban on open burning, and ensuring efficient firefighting operational readiness. Arthur said that although fire incidents were still under control within the respective borders of member states, the risk of transboundary haze called for collective preparedness and heightened vigilance at the regional level.

items.title: Serian API drops to 190 as Sarawak air quality improves slightly
items.summary: Meanwhile, 57 areas nationwide recorded API readings at the moderate level. An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous. API data is released hourly based on readings recorded at 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: No more walk-ins: Malaysia’s foreign worker recruitment now entirely online
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 22 — Applications for the recruitment of foreign workers are now fully processed online through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS), eliminating the need for employers to submit applications manually or make walk-in visits from today The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) said the digitalisation initiative aims to simplify the process by reducing repeated visits to government offices, shortening waiting times and making the overall procedure more organised and transparent. “All applications remain subject to scrutiny, relevant laws, eligibility requirements, foreign worker employment policies and reviews by the relevant Regulatory Agencies (AKS),” it said in a statement. Kesuma said the application process begins with employers obtaining prior approval to hire foreign workers under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955, until the issuance of a Conditional Approval Letter (SKB).

items.title: Terengganu village on alert after wild elephant destroys banana, sugarcane crops
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 22 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is investigating a complaint about a wild elephant reportedly roaming in Kampung Pengkalan Gelugor, Jeram, here yesterday. State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said investigations found that the elephant had destroyed residents’ crops, including banana and sugarcane plants, while also roaming around the village and posing a safety risk to residents. “Residents are also urged to give the department space to carry out control and translocation operations when conditions permit,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Teacher and son die after MPV hits debris and plunges into ravine in Rompin
items.summary: Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the accident, which occurred at about 9.30 pm, claimed the lives of Kartinie Ngatenan, 46, and her six-year-old son Muhammad Akif Mohd Azmi at the scene. He said preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred when the multipurpose vehicle (MPV), driven by the victim’s 47-year-old husband, was travelling from Seremban, Negeri Sembilan, towards Felda Keratong in Rompin. Sharif Shai said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Chew Swee Yoke, Malaysia’s legal aid pioneer and lawyer in Anwar’s ‘black eye’ case, dies at 81
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Chew Swee Yoke, a pioneering Malaysian lawyer, advocate for justice and proud Victorian, passed away on the morning of August 18, aged 81. In 1982, Chew established the first Legal Aid Centre in Kuala Lumpur and became the first Chairperson of the Bar Council Legal Aid Committee. The Malaysian Bar recognises her as a pioneer of legal aid in Malaysia.

items.title: Exco: Perak and federal governments streamlining laws for Pulau Sembilan enforcement
items.summary: SUNGAI SIPUT, Aug 22 — The Perak and federal governments are upgrading existing legislation to streamline and strengthen enforcement operations in the waters of the Pulau Sembilan State Park. Perak Tourism, Industry, Investment and Corridor Development Committee chairman Loh Sze Yee said the move aimed to address overlapping jurisdictions between the two parties, which had made comprehensive enforcement difficult. The Pulau Sembilan State Park was officially closed to the public on April 1, 2017, following severe damage to its marine ecosystem and coral reef structures caused by encroachment and uncontrolled tourism activities.

items.title: Penang police warn convoy participants: No sirens, no stunts, no controlling traffic
items.summary: “The assessment will take into account the route, number of participants, timing, stopover locations and current traffic conditions to ensure the convoy can proceed in an orderly manner without affecting safety, public order and traffic flow,” he said in a statement yesterday. He said organisers and participants must also comply with all laws and road regulations, as well as follow the instructions of police and traffic officers. Lim said organisers must also take into account ongoing construction work, lane closures and traffic diversions when planning the convoy route and timing.

items.title: Thai police detain two Kelantan men for possession of 1,560 Epam pills
items.summary: NARATHIWAT, Aug 22 — Two Malaysians were detained by Thai police in Sungai Kolok here on Thursday night after authorities found 1,560 Epam (Nitrazepam) tablets believed to be in their possession. Sungai Kolok Police Chief Col Thun Sirikhunt, when contacted by Bernama, said the two suspects, aged 24 and 30 and from Kelantan, were detained at about 10.30 pm in front of a restaurant on Jalan Anukachart Usorn in Sungai Kolok town, following intelligence gathering and information from members of the public. Thun said the drugs, classified as a Category 2 psychotropic substance, were packed in 39 blister packs, each containing 40 tablets, with a total estimated value of 10,608 baht (about RM1,310).

items.title: Penang Hospital acts to cut emergency wait times after viral video shows overcrowding
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — The Penang Health Department (JKNPP) is implementing several measures to reduce congestion and waiting times at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Penang Hospital (HPP), particularly during peak hours. Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah said a short-term measure involves upgrading space at the HPP Outpatient Department block to expand treatment areas and integrate patient flow from the Emergency and Trauma Department. “JKNPP takes note of the video that went viral on social media last night regarding the long waiting time at the HPP Emergency and Trauma Department.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan strengthen legal ties with new prisoner transfer treaty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Malaysia and Pakistan yesterday signed the International Transfer of Prisoners (ITOP) Treaty, strengthening legal and security cooperation between the two countries. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the treaty was signed with Pakistan’s Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi following his courtesy call on Pakistan Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. “This signing marks another important milestone in Malaysia-Pakistan bilateral relations, particularly in strengthening security and legal cooperation between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.

items.title: Anwar and Pakistans’s Shehbaz call for diplomacy in Iran-US tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Pakistani counterpart Shehbaz Sharif have agreed that regional tensions must be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy to safeguard peace and stability. Anwar said the shared position was reached during a telephone conversation with Shehbaz, during which they exchanged views on current regional developments and the latest developments in Iran-US relations. In a Facebook post, Anwar said Shehbaz also enquired about his health during the telephone conversation.

items.title: From a Penang home kitchen to nationwide favourite: The story of Jeruk Madu Pak Ali
items.summary: More than four decades later, Jeruk Madu Pak Ali has grown from a three-person operation to a business with four production plants in Simpang Ampat on mainland Penang with over 100 employees and 50 retail outlets nationwide. Together, the facilities produce about 300 tonnes of pickled fruits every month. Jeruk Madu Pak Ali’s marketing and public relations executive Mohd Shahrul Nizam Shahidin showing the packaged pickled fruits and the traditional trades certificate from Penang Global Tourism.

items.title: Tebrau MP to raise in Parliament tax uncertainty over commingled oil cargo
items.summary: He said the matter required clarification from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD) to ensure industry players had clarity and certainty regarding their tax obligations. As such, I hope and urge the Royal Customs to provide greater clarity on this matter to industry players. Puah said he would raise the matter in Parliament to seek clarification on the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo operations.

items.title: Independent review, not blind denial, needed to address US transshipment claims, says maritime trade expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Malaysia should conduct an independent review into allegations by the United States (US) concerning transshipment activities to ensure any violations are identified while protecting the country’s reputation, according to Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. The maritime expert said the review must trace the complete movement of the cargo, including the manifest, bill of lading, Customs documentation, certificate of origin, storage records, any blending or processing carried out and the final declaration before export. “Malaysia must respond quickly with evidence, independent verification and a clear enforcement position.

items.title: Zahid: Melaka election strategy cannot mirror Johor, Negeri Sembilan, needs tailored formula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Barisan Nasional (BN) needs a formula suitable to Melaka’s geopolitical landscape in the upcoming state election, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said any negotiations must take into account two aspects, namely benefits and drawbacks. He said political cooperation at the state level should also be seen in the context of efforts to strengthen political stability at the national level.

items.title: Sarawak haze fight hinges on suitable clouds, Uggah says seeding useless without them
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 21 — Cloud seeding operations to tackle the haze will depend on favourable weather conditions, particularly the presence of suitable clouds, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman said discussions had been held with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), which was ready to conduct the cloud seeding operation whenever weather conditions permit. Uggah expressed hope that weather conditions would improve soon, allowing the cloud seeding operation to be carried out and help tackle the haze.
